issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary’s active participation in executing a will does not, by itself, make the will suspicious or invalidate it when the evidence establishes due execution and attestation and supports the testator’s deliberate disposition.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court found that the will was duly executed and attested and that no circumstances cast doubt on the testatrix’s capacity or free will.
The beneficiaries had actively participated in the execution of the will.

Shortly before execution, the daughter reported that her mother was being abducted and filed a suit claiming title against her, supporting the finding that she knew her mother intended to dispose of the property.

The testatrix executed the will despite the daughter’s efforts to prevent the disposition, later lived with the daughter until her death, and neither complained about the will nor executed another will.
The daughter’s allegation that the beneficiaries procured the will by fraud was not substantiated, and the High Court dismissed the second appeal because it raised no question of law.
issues.conclusion: The active participation of the beneficiaries was not sufficient, in the circumstances, to cast doubt on the will. The concurrent findings that the will was genuine and intended to be acted upon were upheld, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principles in H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B.N. Thimmajamma, Smt. Jaswant Kaur v. Smt. Amrit Kaur, and Smt. Indu Bala Bose v. Manindra Chandra Bose, the propounder must establish the will and remove genuine suspicious circumstances; active participation by a beneficiary may be relevant but does not alone establish such suspicion. The Court also noted that the High Court had dismissed the second appeal because there was no question of law attracting Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

rule.if: appeal_from_concurrent_will_findings and will_execution_and_attestation_proved and beneficiary_active_in_execution and deliberate_disposition_supported and testator_lived_with_challenger_after_execution and no_complaint_or_revocation and no_other_circumstances_doubting_capacity_or_free_will

predicates.appeal_from_concurrent_will_findings: The proceeding challenges concurrent lower-court findings about the proof or genuineness of a will.
predicates.will_execution_and_attestation_proved: The evidence establishes that the testator executed the will and that it was properly attested.
predicates.beneficiary_active_in_execution: A person who benefits under the will took an active part in its execution.
predicates.deliberate_disposition_supported: The surrounding evidence supports that the testator knowingly intended the disposition, including the exclusion of a close relative.
predicates.testator_lived_with_challenger_after_exe: After executing the will, the testator lived with the person challenging it.
predicates.no_complaint_or_revocation: The testator made no complaint about the will and did not revoke or replace it before death.
predicates.no_other_circumstances_doubting_capacity: No other evidence casts doubt on the testator’s testamentary capacity or freedom of choice.

issues.definition: When a challenge to concurrent findings about a will is supported by proof of execution and attestation, evidence of a deliberate disposition, and the testator’s subsequent conduct without other circumstances casting doubt on capacity or free will, active participation by a beneficiary alone does not prevent the will from being found genuine.
